    Step 2 · Practice · Skill: MAF & allele frequencies

    Math drills — “to the T”

    Three moves, step by step. Every human is diploid, so people × 2 = alleles. Every drill shows its numbers on a dbSNP card in the exact format of the lecture slide (the worked example below) — same layout every time, so finding the (1000Genomes) row becomes automatic. Type your answer for instant feedback, tap Hint for one step at a time, and open the full worked solution after you answer.

    Move 1
    major = 1 − MAF
    Major frequency from minor.
    Move 2
    frequency = count ÷ (people × 2)
    Count → frequency.
    Move 3
    count = frequency × (people × 2)
    Frequency → expected count.
    Fresh problem • —

    Press “New problem” to start.

    Reference visual — the lecture slide every MAF question copies

    This is the dbSNP teaching slide for rs1442. The annotations point at the SNP ID, the alleles (G>C), the locus, and the gene name (TGFBI). The MAF list is where every number question comes from: find the (1000Genomes) row — C = 0.3177 / 1591. Frequency before the slash, count after it.

    Reference — the setup rules from Poll 1

    The professor's rules, literally: 1) the allele named in the question goes in the numerator of the odds ratio. 2) In each odds fraction, the disease count goes on top. 3) Odds are counts, not totals — 1 with / 50 without is 1/50, never 1/51. 4) Sanity-check first: eyeball which allele's carriers get sick more often, then make the math agree. And Han Solo's rule: never judge one allele's odds alone — only the ratio means anything.

    Step 3 · Check

    Exam Practice — the lecture's questions, new numbers

    The polls, remixed: questions rotate through every poll family — codon classification, coverage, the dbSNP major-allele question, frequency ↔ count conversions, and three-allele MAF — shuffled so you never get a long run of one kind, with fresh numbers and drawings each time. Codon questions include the codon chart, and their right answers rotate too (missense, synonymous, nonsense, noncoding). Coverage questions come with a fresh cartoon drawing — count the reads stacked over the marked position. Every MAF question shows its dbSNP card in the exact format of the lecture slide — and each question names which study’s row to read (1000Genomes, gnomAD, TOPMed, PAGE Study, Vietnamese, HapMap, ALFA…), so find that row first, then do the math. Stuck? Tap Hint for one step at a time; the full worked solution appears after you answer.
